item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Project Operations - Perform bulk operations for bookings on schedule board
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to move or reassign multiple bookings at once, directly from the schedule board in Dynamics 365 Project Operations. This feature will reach public preview on September 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature eliminates repetitive, manual edits required during common scenarios such as resource replacement, timeline shifts, scope changes, or schedule realignments. The feature significantly reduces administrative effort and helps you respond quickly to change and manage large teams and complex projects at scale. This feature lets you:
  • Select multiple blocks of bookings and bookable resources on the schedule board.
  • Move all the selected blocks by the required number of days.
  • Reassign multiple bookings to another bookable resource.
  • Move and reassign operations directly on the schedule board.
What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Perform bulk operations for bookings on schedule board.

item.title: [planForChange] Browser Use Admin Control for Copilot Cowork
item.description:
[What and why:]

Controls for browser use in Copilot Cowork are now available in the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC). As part of this rollout, we're also introducing more granular access controls, allowing admins to enable the capability for specific users or security groups instead of managing access at the tenant-wide level. This gives organizations greater flexibility to run controlled pilots, validate the experience with targeted teams, and expand access over time.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid-September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Admins can configure local browser access for:

  • No users
  • All users
  • Specific groups
  • Only users included in the configured scope will have access to the capability

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Review which users or security groups should receive access and plan how you'll evaluate the capability. Consider starting with a small pilot group before expanding deployment more broadly.

Tenant admins must enable Cowork browsing by performing the following steps. This feature is disabled by default.

  1. From the menu, select Copilot > Settings > View All > Cowork settings.
  2. Under Allow browser access, select Allow Cowork to use the Microsoft Edge browser to perform tasks on behalf of users.
  3. Use the local browser with Copilot Cowork | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [planForChange] In-app browsing in Copilot app
item.description:
[What and why:]

We are adding support to the Microsoft Copilot app, in Windows and Mac, to allow websites that Copilot shares in chat to open inside of the desktop app side by side with the Copilot chat conversation. This is available now but not available by default; administrators can opt-in selected Windows and Mac devices to test this.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • Opt-in availability: Available now.
  • Broader rollout: Begins late November 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Administrators can manage early access by opting-in selected devices and deploying the updates via instructions linked below. This early access allows you to:

  • Test in-app browsing at your organization before the broader rollout. This allows users to open links within the Copilot desktop app.
  • Validate deployed and in-app browsing behavior in your organization's managed environment.
  • Prepare support teams and users for the updated experience that applies to Copilot Windows and Mac endpoints.

What users will see

When a user clicks a link within the Copilot desktop app, the website opens in a side pane to the right of the Copilot chat. Users can open multiple links, each appearing as a separate tab within the side pane and can switch between tabs as needed. Once the websites are no longer needed, users can close the side pane.

Users can adjust the in-app browser side pane to be smaller or larger. They can also enter full-screen mode to view the website in a full-screen experience and can toggle in and out of this mode using the button in the side pane header.

Users can still open a link in an external browser, by:

  • Selecting the "External browser" option from the three-dot menu on the link within Copilot Chat
  • OR Selecting “Copy the URL” and pasting it into an external browser
  • OR Right clicking a tab in the side pane within the Copilot app and selecting "External browser" (coming 9/21)

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • To enable in-app browsing, you can turn on the 'BrowsingEnabled' policy through your device management system.
    • Microsoft Edge Browser Policy Documentation | Microsoft Learn
    • Configure Microsoft Edge for Windows with policy settings | Microsoft Learn
  • Review the in-app browsing associated policies that can be adjusted and changed.

[Compliance Considerations:]

  • Does the change store new customer data? Yes. Browsing history, cookies, autofill information are stored on the local device. This follows the same storage mechanisms as Microsoft Edge storing data in the user Data profile directory at “%localappdata%\Microsoft\Copilot\User Data”.
  • Does the change provide end users with a new way of interacting with generative AI? This feature does not add any new way to create or steer generative AI, it only lets you view websites, whether those are website on the internet or html files created generatively with copilot via other features.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) OneDrive for Business: Improved Windows Desktop sync error messages for max path length
item.description:
Updated September 18, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

We are improving the OneDrive sync experience on Windows desktop to provide clearer, more actionable guidance when file and folder paths exceed the supported 520-character limit. The updated experience will show exactly how many characters a path exceeds the limit and will provide a guided flow to rename or move affected items so they can sync successfully.

This improvement addresses a common OneDrive sync issue by reducing user confusion, minimizing workflow disruption, and helping users resolve errors faster.

This update is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557563.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning by early October 2026 (previously mid-September) and expected to complete by end of October 2026 (previously mid-October)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • All users of the OneDrive sync client on Windows desktop

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Business (Windows desktop sync client)

What will happen

Max path errors are one of the most commonly reported issues by OneDrive sync users. Currently, when a file or folder path exceeds the 520-character sync limit, the error message only states how many characters the path exceeds the limit and asks users to shorten it. In addition, File Explorer limitations may prevent users from renaming paths over 260 characters, and the sync client may stop syncing until the issue is resolved.

As part of this improved error experience, when users encounter max path errors, the sync client will continue running and users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience.

With this update:

  • The sync client will continue running when users encounter max path errors
  • Users will be guided through a custom rename and move experience to resolve issues directly

The rename experience will:

  • Show the number of over-limit characters
  • Highlight which items in the path can be renamed
  • Allow renames even when the path exceeds 260 characters

Screenshot - Custom rename dialog

The move experience will:

  • Show over-limit character counts in a guided interface
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit shared items in OneDrive
  • Display warning dialogs for over-limit items in shortcuts

Screenshot - Example warning dialog for overlimit items in shortcuts

These enhancements are designed to reduce troubleshooting time and improve the overall sync experience.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. This update will be automatically available through the OneDrive sync client.

You may want to:

  • Inform your helpdesk and support teams about the improved error messages, as this update should reduce max-path-related support tickets.
  • Update internal documentation for resolving OneDrive sync issues if applicable.

Learn more

  • Fix paths that are too long to sync in OneDrive | Microsoft Support
  • Restrictions and limitations in OneDrive and SharePoint | Microsoft Support

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. This update does not change how customer data is stored, processed, or accessed.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: New centralized experience for organizing important resources in chats and channels
item.description:

[What and why]

We are introducing a more consistent way for users to access and manage important resources in Microsoft Teams chats and channels. Users will be able to pin frequently used resources directly below the chat or channel header, pin multiple messages alongside other resources, and organize them into folders. On Microsoft Teams mobile, users will be able to access shared resources and folders by tapping the chat or channel header. This change will help users stay organized and provide them with a centralized location to quickly find, access, and manage important resources.

As part of this update, the In this chat and In this channel panes will be removed. Existing resources within these panes will be accessible through the new resource management experience.

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Rollout begins in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who access or manage resources in Microsoft Teams chats and channels.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft Teams mobile

What will happen

  • Users will have a centralized location to find, access, and manage important resources.
  • Users will be able to pin frequently used resources directly below the chat or channel header, pin multiple messages alongside other resources, and organize them into folders.
  • On mobile devices, users will be able to access shared resources and folders by tapping the chat or channel header.
  • The In this chat and In this channel panes will be removed; existing resources within these panes will be accessed and managed through the updated experience.

Screenshot - Comparison before and after

No administrative action is required. We recommend that you:

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] (Updated) Microsoft Exchange Online: Review and configure EWSAllowedAppIDs before Exchange Web Services access changes
item.description:
Updated September 18, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

As part of the final phase of Exchange Web Services (EWS) retirement, Microsoft is updating how the EWSAllowedAppIDs setting is applied in Exchange Online. This change is designed to help organizations identify and manage applications that still require EWS access while reducing the risk of unexpected service disruption.

Organizations that continue to use EWS should review and maintain their own EWSAllowedAppIDs list. If a tenant administrator has already configured this list, Microsoft will not overwrite or modify it.

Beginning on October 1, 2026, Microsoft will start enabling this updated behavior by cloud as part of the EWS retirement rollout.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD: Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by late April 2027

The updated behavior will apply when the rollout reaches your cloud.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that continue to use Exchange Web Services (EWS)
  • Exchange Online administrators responsible for managing EWS access
  • Tenants with EWSEnabled set to True or Null

Platforms and services

  • Exchange Online
  • Exchange Web Services (EWS)

What will happen

After the updated behavior is enabled in a cloud:

  • EWS will require a configured EWSAllowedAppIDs list when EWSEnabled is set to True.
  • Before enabling the change, Microsoft will ensure that tenants with EWSEnabled already set to True have an EWSAllowedAppIDs list.
  • If a customer-managed list does not exist, Microsoft will generate a list based on EWS application usage observed during the previous 60 days to help reduce the risk of service interruption.
  • Microsoft-generated lists may omit applications that run infrequently and may include applications that no longer require EWS access.
  • If EWSEnabled remains Null, Microsoft will populate EWSAllowedAppIDs only when a customer-managed list does not already exist. This will occur shortly before Microsoft updates EWSEnabled to False as part of the retirement rollout.
  • Microsoft will not modify an EWSAllowedAppIDs list that has already been configured by a tenant administrator.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization still relies on EWS, we recommend taking the following actions as soon as possible:

  • Review EWS usage from the previous 60 days and identify all applications that require continued EWS access, including applications with infrequent usage patterns.
  • Configure and validate your EWSAllowedAppIDs list before the rollout reaches your cloud.
  • Ensure EWSEnabled is set to True if continued EWS access is required.
  • Keep the EWSAllowedAppIDs list current as applications are added, removed, or migrated away from EWS.
  • Plan for up to a 24-hour propagation delay after changes are made to the EWSAllowedAppIDs list.

Microsoft's safeguard helps reduce the risk of service disruption but does not replace customer review and validation of EWSAllowedAppIDs.

We also recommend continuing plans to migrate applications from EWS to Microsoft Graph before EWS retirement is completed.

Learn more

  • Deprecation of Exchange Web Services in Exchange Online | Microsoft Learn
  • Introducing EWSAllowedAppIDs: Preparing for the Final Phase of EWS Retirement

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform - Information regarding the end of support for Global Discovery Service (GDS) API
item.description:
On September 21, 2026, the Global Discovery Service (GDS) API will have reached end of support.

How does this affect me?
The legacy Global Discovery Service (GDS) REST API endpoints hosted at globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com will no longer be available.

Deprecated GDS endpoints:
  • https://globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com/api/discovery/v1.0/Instances
  • https://globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com/api/discovery/v2.0/Instances
  • https://globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com/api/discovery/v1.0/Instances({id})
This change impacts listing and retrieval of Dataverse organizations. There is no impact to service performance or availability for your environment(s)

Please note that this end of support change excludes the Dataverse Developer Tools such as CRM SDK and Connectors.

What action do I need to take?
  1. Identify any applications or scripts that call globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com REST API endpoints.
  2. Update your applications to use the Power Platform List Environments API instead of the GDS endpoints.
  3. Test your updated integrations against the new endpoints to verify compatibility.
Please note that the Power Platform API uses a different token audience than GDS. You will need to update your authentication to request tokens with the scope (https://api.powerplatform.com/.default) and register the Power Platform API (app ID 8578e004-a5c6-46e7-913e-12f58912df43) as an API permission in your Microsoft Entra app registration. For detailed setup instructions, see Power Platform API Authentication.

To avoid a disruption in service, please migrate to the Power Platform List Environments API before September 21, 2026.

If you need additional assistance, please contact Microsoft Support.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot: SpaceXAI subprocessor admin setting
item.description:
[What and why:]

As part of our efforts to expand model choice in Copilot, SpaceXAI has been added to Microsoft's Online Services Subprocessor List, published in the Service Trust Portal. Being listed as a subprocessor does not, by itself, mean SpaceXAI is enabled for your organization or that SpaceXAI is processing your data.

Access to Grok models is governed by a new SpaceXAI admin setting under AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The setting is disabled by default. Eligible customers participating in Frontier must explicitly enable the setting before Grok models can be used in their organization. If enabled, Grok models will be available in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Users can select Grok from the model selector when using Copilot in those apps.

When the SpaceXAI setting is enabled, Microsoft’s Product Terms and Data Protection Addendum (DPA) apply to the use of Grok models, except as otherwise disclosed in Microsoft Learn documentation.

[Rollout schedule:]

The SpaceXAI setting to enable the use of Grok models in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint will be available to eligible customers starting September 18, 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Customers participating in Frontier are eligible to access Grok models in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Note: The following customers are not eligible and won’t see the SpaceXAI admin setting during initial rollout even if participating in Frontier.
  • Tenants in the EU, EFTA, and the UK.
  • Government cloud customers (GCC, GCC High, DoD).
  • Administrators managing model access controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • The SpaceXAI admin setting will become available to eligible Frontier customers and will be disabled by default. Grok models are not available, and no customer data will be processed by SpaceXAI, unless an admin enables it.
  • If the admin setting is enabled, users will be able to select a Grok model from the model selector when using Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Admins can scope access to specific users or groups.
  • There is no change for organizations that take no action.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • Review Microsoft Learn page covering SpaceXAI as a subprocessor and the new administrative setting.
  • Decide whether to enable the SpaceXAI setting for your organization and determine whether to scope access to specific users or groups.
  • Review published compliance information, including SpaceXAI's via the SpaceXAI Trust Center, and confirm it aligns with your organization's requirements before enabling access.
  • Notify your helpdesk and compliance teams if your organization has specific requirements around third-party model providers.

[Compliance considerations:]

Compliance areaImpact
AI/ML or agent capabilitiesIntroduces Grok models as a model option in Copilot for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Admin controlsA new SpaceXAI admin setting lets admins enable or disable access, with user- and group-level scoping. It is disabled by default.
Data processingSpaceXAI is listed as a Microsoft AI subprocessor. No processing occurs unless the setting is enabled.
Regional availabilityOnly available to Frontier Public customers – not available to customers in the EU, EFTA, or UK at this time, or to government clouds.
Third-party certificationsSOC 1 Type II, PCI, FedRAMP and HITRUST certifications are not currently available for SpaceXAI. Customers should review available certification information before enabling access. Refer to SpaceXAI’s own certification landing page to understand the availability of their certifications, additional exclusions, and audit reports.

  2. SpaceXAI as a subprocessor in Microsoft Online Services
  3. Understanding AI functionality and models in Microsoft Online Services

item.title: [planForChange] Retirement of Microsoft 365 Companion apps
item.description:
[What and why:]

The Microsoft 365 companion apps—Calendar, People, and Files — are taskbar-integrated apps designed to streamline everyday workflows, helping users stay focused, reduce context switching, and complete tasks faster. 

We are retiring the companion apps, and they will no longer function or be supported after 16. December 2026. We advise admins remove the apps from devices in their tenant by this date. Detailed admin guidance is in Microsoft 365 companion app retirement.

[Rollout schedule:]

Microsoft 365 companion apps will reach end of life on December 16, 2026.

  • As of the publication of this message, Microsoft will begin phasing out automatic installation of the companion apps. Updates and fixes, including security fixes, are no longer being provided. Existing installations can continue to function during the retirement window.
  • December 16, 2026: Remaining companion apps will stop functioning and will no longer be supported.

[Impact on your organization:]

This retirement affects worldwide enterprise customers that installed the apps.

Microsoft will stop the automatic installation of companion apps through Microsoft 365 Apps updates. Admins must prevent new installations through other deployment methods and should remove existing installations from managed devices. Users of unmanaged devices should uninstall the apps themselves.

The companion apps were an additional way to find calendar information, people, and files so removing them will not delete or impact any existing capabilities or Microsoft 365 data.

Users can continue finding calendar information, people, and files using existing Microsoft 365 and Windows experiences such as Outlook, Teams, Windows Search Box, File Explorer, SharePoint, OneDrive, and more.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Admins will need to take steps such as letting users know the companion apps are being retired, stopping deployment of new installations, removing existing installations, and removing references from all internal documentation, guides, communications, and training materials.

Review the retirement article linked above for all the steps you need to take.

If you encounter an issue that may require an update or fix during the retirement period, see the guidance in the Troubleshooting section in the retirement article.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Planner: Capacity view
item.description:
[What and why]

Capacity view is a new view in Planner that presents a live staffing matrix built from existing Planner task data. It shows a timeline of who is working on what, so team leads can see how work is distributed across the team and spot overallocation or open capacity at a glance, without exporting data or building a separate report. This keeps resource decisions in the same tool where the work is already tracked.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by mid-October 2026
  • General availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with a Planner Plan 3 license in Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) environments 
  • Users without a Plan 3 license will not see Capacity view

Platforms and services

  • Planner in Teams (web and desktop)
  • Planner in Outlook (web and desktop)
  • Capacity view is not included on mobile

What will happen

  • Capacity view appears as a new view on existing plans, alongside Board, Grid, and Schedule.
  • The view is populated entirely from existing Planner task data. No new data is created.
  • Accuracy depends on tasks having assignees and start and finish dates. Tasks missing either will not be represented reliably in the timeline.
  • The view is on by default for eligible users and there is no admin control to disable it. 

[Action required and recommendations]

  • No admin action is required to enable or prepare for this change. To get value from the view, consider the following:
  • Notify Planner users that a new Capacity view will appear on their plans in early October 2026.
  • Update internal training material and Planner guidance to include the new view.
  • Encourage plan owners and team leads to keep assignees and start and finish dates current so the view reflects actual workload.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Entra ID: Follow-up on SMS first-factor sign-in retirement and upcoming changes
item.description:
[What and why]

To improve security and reduce reliance on vulnerable authentication methods, Microsoft is continuing the retirement of SMS first-factor sign-in in Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, as the preferred sign-in experience because they help reduce the risk of phishing, fraud, and account compromise associated with phone-based authentication.

Microsoft previously retired SMS first-factor sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants and stopped enabling SMS sign-in for newly created tenants. This communication provides an update on the next phase of the retirement effort and actions organizations should take to prepare. Microsoft has announced previous retirement actions in Message Center posts MC1426371, MC1448374, and MC1449181.

This retirement applies only to Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenant authentication scenarios. It does not apply to Azure AD B2C or Microsoft Entra External ID customer identity scenarios.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide and GCC: Beginning February 1, 2027, SMS first-factor sign-in will be retired for Microsoft Entra ID tenants.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

Organizations that:

  • Allow users to sign in using SMS first-factor authentication.
  • Rely on SMS first-factor sign-in as a primary authentication method.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • SMS first-factor passwordless sign-in (SignInNoPassword)

What will happen

After February 1, 2027:

  • Users will no longer be able to authenticate by using their phone number and an SMS one-time passcode as a primary sign-in method.
  • Existing SMS first-factor sign-in configurations will no longer be honored.
  • Management and configuration experiences for SMS first-factor sign-in will be removed from Microsoft administration experiences.
  • Attempts to sign in by using a registered phone number and SMS one-time passcode will be blocked.
  • Users who have another registered authentication method can continue signing in.
  • Organizations that do not migrate affected users before the retirement date may experience sign-in disruptions.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization uses SMS first-factor sign-in, complete the following actions before February 1, 2027:

  • Identify users currently using SMS first-factor sign-in.
  • Ensure affected users register an alternative authentication method before February 1, 2027.
  • Communicate this change to affected users to prevent sign-in disruptions.
  • Migrate users to passkeys or other phishing-resistant authentication methods.
  • Review authentication method policies and remove dependencies on SMS first-factor sign-in.
  • Review available authentication alternatives and migration guidance.

The retirement of SMS sign-in as a first-factor authentication method applies even when you use Choose Your Own Telephony Provider to continue using SMS or voice as multifactor authentication method. If your organization currently uses SMS sign-in for first-factor authentication, migrate users to supported alternatives based on their scenarios. Alternatives include passkeys, QR code authentication, FIDO2 security keys, and other authentication methods supported by Microsoft Entra ID.

Learn more

  • SMS-based user sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change modify how users access Microsoft 365 resources or services?Users who currently rely on SMS first-factor authentication must use another registered authentication method after February 1, 2027.
Does this change require admin action to maintain user access?Administrators should identify affected users and ensure alternative authentication methods are registered before the retirement date.
Does this change affect Conditional Access policies?Organizations may need to review authentication-related policies and dependencies that currently rely on SMS first-factor sign-in.
Does this change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Management and configuration experiences for SMS first-factor sign-in will be removed from Microsoft Entra administration experiences.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Existing SMS first-factor sign-in configurations will no longer be honored after the retirement date, requiring administrators to transition users to supported authentication methods.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot app: Branded footer customization
item.description:
Updated September 17, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

We’re introducing a new co-branding capability that will allow organizations to display a branded footer at the bottom of the Chat screen in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app. This update will enable admins to add their organization’s logo to their users’ Microsoft 365 Copilot app, helping users confirm they are using their trusted, work-managed Copilot experience.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 555852.

[When this will happen]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out August 2026 (previously mid-July) and is expected to complete by mid-September 2026 (previously end of July).

[How this will affect your organization]

Who is affected

  • All Microsoft 365 tenants using the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.

What will happen

  • Admins will be able to upload a logo in the Microsoft 365 admin center to customize the footer in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • The footer will use the same logo configured in your organization’s theme for other Microsoft 365 apps. Only the logo will be used; other theme settings will not apply in this release.

  • Admins can choose a footer label: Approved by, Provided by, or Managed by. Selecting No label will display the logo without a label.
  • This feature will be off by default and will require admin configuration.
  • There will be no user impact unless an admin enables the footer.

[What you can do to prepare]

No action will be required unless you want to enable the branded footer.

Admins who want to configure this feature should:

  • In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Org settings > Custom theme and open your default theme.
  • Confirm that your organization’s logo is configured in the Logos tab. This is the same logo used for your organization’s branding in other Microsoft 365 apps.
  • Open the Copilot Chat tab and select Add your brand to Copilot Chat footer area.
  • In the Footer style dropdown, choose No label, Approved by, Provided by, or Managed by.
  • Save your changes to display your logo in the branded footer in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.

Please note: The footer currently uses your organization's default theme and applies to all users. Targeting different logos to specific user groups will be supported in a later update.

For configuration guidance: Customize the theme for your organization | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Edge: IE mode is supported through at least the end of 2029, plan your migration
item.description:
[What and why] 

Internet Explorer (IE) mode in Microsoft Edge remains supported through at least the end of 2029, as first announced in 2021. Microsoft is sharing this reminder so admins can plan migrations for legacy websites and applications that still depend on IE mode. Application modernization projects can take years to complete depending on the number and complexity of dependencies, so early planning reduces the risk of disruption later.

[Rollout schedule]

This is a reminder, not a rollout of a new feature or capability. IE mode support continues through at least the end of 2029 across Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD environments. Microsoft will provide at least one year of notice before retiring IE mode.

[Impact on your organization]

item.title: [planForChange] Brand Skill support now available in PPT Copilot [Desktop]
item.description:
[What and why:]

Brand managers will be able to upload custom presentation skills as Markdown (.md) files to Brand Kit and share them across their organization for use with Copilot in PowerPoint. This capability helps organizations provide reusable, organization-approved instructions that guide presentation creation, supporting more consistent and efficient content development.

This change advances personal and team productivity by embedding reusable presentation guidance into the tools employees use to create presentations.

[Rollout schedule:]

Frontier: We will begin rolling out mid-September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

General Availability, Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in late September 2026 and expect to complete by the end of September 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Brand managers who create, manage, and publish organizational Brand Kits.
  • Users in organizations where a Brand Kit containing a custom presentation skill has been published and who have access to Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • The product team should confirm applicable licensing and whether additional eligibility requirements apply.

Platforms and services:

  • Microsoft 365 Brand Kit
  • Microsoft Copilot
  • Microsoft PowerPoint - Desktop

What will happen:

  • Brand managers will be able to upload a custom presentation skill as a Markdown (.md) or .zip file to Brand Kit.
  • Brand managers will be able to publish the skill for use by people in their organization.
  • Eligible users will be able to use the published skill with Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • The skill can provide reusable instructions to guide how Copilot creates presentations.
  • The feature requires a Brand manager to upload and publish a skill. It is not automatically activated merely because the capability becomes available.

[Action required and recommendations:]

  • Review who is assigned as a Brand manager through the Enterprise Brand Manager policy.
  • Identify the people responsible for writing, reviewing, approving, and maintaining presentation skills.
  • Establish governance for security, privacy, accessibility, legal, and brand review.
  • Test skills with representative presentation scenarios before publishing them broadly.
  • Communicate the availability of published skills to users of Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • Update internal Brand Kit and Copilot documentation.
  • Review published skills periodically and remove or replace outdated instructions.
  • Review Microsoft documentation: Brand Skill support for Copilot in PowerPoint.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • This change provides eligible users with a new way to interact with generative AI by using organization-published instructions with Copilot in PowerPoint.
  • This change introduces organization-published instructions that can guide Copilot when users create presentations.
  • Brand Kit publishing is governed through the Enterprise Brand Manager policy and a mail-enabled security group. Confirm that presentation skills use the same controls without additional configuration.
  • Confirm storage, retention, audit logging, Purview behavior, user-level disablement, third-party integration, and GDPR data-subject-request implications before publication.

Viva Engage will stop sending email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination. Previously, email notifications could still be attempted for these users, resulting in repeated delivery retries, increased load on email systems, and, in some cases, delays to important business communications.

This change reduces unnecessary email traffic, improves delivery efficiency, and helps ensure important communications are delivered reliably and on time.

Users with supported mailbox configurations, including cloud mailboxes, on-premises mailboxes, shared mailboxes, and other routable email destinations, will continue to receive Viva Engage email notifications as expected.

Notifications delivered through supported channels such as Microsoft Teams remain unaffected.

[When this will happen:]

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Microsoft 365 admins managing Viva Engage users and mailbox configurations.

What will happen:

  • Viva Engage will no longer attempt to send email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Users with cloud, on-premises, shared, or other supported mailbox configurations will continue to receive email notifications as expected.
  • This change does not affect the existing email notification experience for users with a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Notifications delivered through Microsoft Teams or other supported channels are not impacted.
  • The change is enabled by default and applies automatically.
  • Organizations may see:
    • Reduced load on email systems and gateways.
    • Fewer retry attempts for undeliverable messages.
    • Improved email delivery efficiency and reliability.

[What you can do to prepare:]

  • No action is required.
  • Review your Exchange Online licensing configuration to identify users without mailbox access.
  • Evaluate your notification strategy (e.g., Teams vs. Email) for frontline workers.
  • Inform helpdesk and user support teams of the expected behavior change.
  • Update internal documentation if email notifications are referenced for frontline users.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint: Guide Presentation Creation with Notes Steering and Strict Brand Adherence
item.description:
[What and why:]

We're introducing two new Brand Kit template settings in Microsoft 365 that help organizations create more consistent, on-brand presentations with Copilot in PowerPoint.

Strict brand adherence (Strict Mode) allows Brand Managers to control whether Copilot can create new layouts or must use only approved template and slide master layouts. When enabled, Copilot follows the template exactly and does not add or remove placeholders or create new layouts.

Allow note instructions (Notes Steering) enables Brand Managers to add instructions directly in template speaker notes to guide how Copilot generates presentations. For example, organizations can instruct Copilot to always include a specific slide, preserve branded content, maintain slide order, control text density, or tailor content for a specific audience

These settings can be used independently or together to help organizations generate more predictable, consistent, and brand-aligned presentations.

[Rollout schedule:]

Available now.

[Impact on your organization:]

These capabilities give organizations greater control over how Copilot creates presentations from branded templates.

With Notes Steering, organizations can embed reusable guidance directly into templates, helping ensure presentations consistently follow branding, messaging, and content requirements without requiring users to repeat instructions in every prompt. With Strict Mode enabled, Copilot uses only approved template layouts and slide masters, helping organizations maintain presentation standards and reduce deviations from approved brand designs. This is especially valuable for customer-facing, executive, regulatory, or other business-critical presentations where brand consistency is important.

Together, these settings help deliver more predictable, on-brand PowerPoint presentations while reducing manual editing and review effort.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

No action is required to use these capabilities.

However, organizations that want greater control over presentation generation should designate Brand Managers and ensure they have permissions to manage Brand Kits. Only Brand Kit owners and Brand Managers can configure template settings such as Strict Brand Adherence and Allow Note Instructions.

To take advantage of these capabilities, Brand Managers can update existing Brand Kit templates or upload new templates configured with Notes Steering and Strict Mode settings.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication
item.description:
Updated September 15, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

Passkeys became the default authentication experience in Microsoft Entra on September 1, 2026. Telecom-based methods (SMS and voice) will transition to customer-configured providers through the Microsoft Security Store.

The AI era demands stronger, phishing-resistant authentication. We are making passkeys the default authentication experience in Microsoft Entra to help customers securely adopt AI at scale.

As part of this transition, SMS and voice will no longer be available as multifactor authentication methods starting February 1, 2027. SMS and voice do not offer sufficient levels of security in comparison to passkeys. Traditional authentication methods including passwords, SMS one-time passcodes, and voice-based verification remain vulnerable to phishing, interception, and social engineering attacks.

We strongly recommend moving away from telephony-based authentication methods to improve security and prevent identity attacks. Passkeys are included in all Microsoft Entra plans, so making this critical security change comes at no additional cost for you.

While we recommend adopting passkeys for phishing-resistant authentication as quickly as possible, we also recognize that some customers may have business needs that make an immediate transition impractical. In such cases, customers may continue to use SMS and voice by selecting a telecom provider in the Microsoft Security Store.

[Rollout schedule]

  1. September 1, 2026: Rollout began. Changes may take time to reach all tenants and will be deployed gradually.
  2. Passkeys will be automatically enabled for users currently enabled for SMS or voice.
  3. Registration Campaign will be set to Microsoft-Managed targeting passkeys for all users in eligible tenants.
  4. Users will be prompted to register a passkey during MFA sign-in; users will be able to skip.
  5. September 18th, 2026:
  6. Review the telecom providers and related information available through the Microsoft Security Store to evaluate which option best meets your regional and compliance requirements.
  7. October 30, 2026:
  8. Customers who need to continue to use SMS or voice will be able to choose from a list of telecom providers available through the Microsoft Security Store.
  9. February 1, 2027:
  10. Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will be retired.
  11. Only customer-configured telecom providers will support SMS and voice going forward.
  12. Passkeys become the default, recommended authentication method.
  13. July 1, 2027:
  14. Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will be retired for Global Admins and external users
  15. Only customer-configured telecom providers will support SMS and voice for these users going forward

If no action is taken, tenants relying only on Microsoft-provided SMS or voice may experience sign-in disruptions after February 1, 2027.


[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  1. All Microsoft Entra ID tenants enabled for SMS or voice authentication
  2. Users enabled for SMS or voice

Platforms and services

  1. Microsoft Entra ID
  2. Multifactor authentication
  3. Microsoft Security Store

What will happen

  1. Passkeys will be automatically enabled for eligible users and Registration Campaign for passkeys will be set to Microsoft Managed state starting September 1, 2026.
  2. Users will be prompted during MFA sign-in to register a passkey; users can skip the prompt.
  3. Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will be retired for most users on February 1, 2027, and for Global Administrators and external users on July 1, 2027.
  4. Organizations that still require telephony methods must configure a telecom provider in the Microsoft Security Store.
  5. Tenants that do not configure a provider and continue relying on Microsoft telephony will face SMS and voice authentication disruptions after retirement.

[Action required and recommendations]

Admins should take the following steps:

  1. Prepare for passkeys
  2. Plan to transition users to passkeys and communicate upcoming registration prompts.
  3. Decide if SMS or voice is still required
  4. If SMS or voice is still needed, you must configure a customer-managed telecom provider. We recommend completing setup at least 4 weeks before the February 1 enforcement to allow sufficient time for testing and a cautious transition.
  5. Set up a telecom provider before February 1, 2027
  6. SMS and voice will only work after this date if a customer-configured telecom provider is enabled.
  7. Use temporary opt-out if needed
  8. A temporary opt-out will be available for the September 1, 2026 through February 1, 2027 changes. This allows you to delay passkey and Registration Campaign enablement while you complete transition activities, such as configuring customer-managed telecom providers or migrating to other authentication methods.
  9. After February 1, 2027, passkey enablement will be enforced for all users in scope.

Additional documentation and more information will be available on Microsoft Learn and the Tech Community.

For more information please visit: https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/concept-sms-voice-retirement more

item.title: [planForChange] [Whiteboard] Legacy Whiteboard migration to OneDrive
item.description:
Updated September 15, 2026: This message does not apply to Government customers. We apologize for the confusion, and you can safely disregard this message.

[What and why:]

Microsoft Whiteboard is completing its transition from legacy Azure-backed storage to OneDrive-backed Whiteboards. Organizations that still have legacy Azure-based Whiteboards must migrate them to OneDrive-backed storage before migration tooling is retired - September 25, 2026. After September 25, 2026, remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated and can be only exported until October 16, 2026. After October 16, 2026, any remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.

Key dates

  1. Before September 25, 2026: Users can still trigger migration, retry failed migrations, and export important content.
  2. September 25, 2026: Migration tooling is retired. Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated, but can still be viewed and exported until October 16, 2026.
  3. October 16, 2026: Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards are permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
  4. November 30, 2026: Legacy Azure Whiteboard service shuts down.

[Rollout schedule:]

Worldwide: We will begin rolling out on late September 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

This change impacts organizations that still have legacy Azure-based Microsoft Whiteboards that have not yet been migrated to OneDrive-backed storage.

After September 25, 2026:

  • Users will no longer be able to migrate remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards.
  • Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated, but can still be viewed and exported until October 16, 2026.
  • Organizations that have not completed migration risk losing access to business content stored in legacy Whiteboards.

After October 16, 2026:

  • Any remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
  • Enterprise users should access Microsoft Whiteboard through Teams and supported web experiences.

Organizations that have already completed migration to OneDrive-backed Whiteboards will not experience changes to existing OneDrive-backed content. New Whiteboards are already created in OneDrive-backed storage.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Admins should take the following actions immediately:

  • Inventory remaining legacy Whiteboards: Use the WhiteboardAdmin PowerShell module to identify Azure-based Whiteboards that still require migration.
  • Communicate with affected users:
  • Notify Whiteboard owners of the migration deadline (September 25, 2026) and deletion deadline (October 16, 2026).
  • Encourage users to migrate, export, or preserve any business-critical content before the deadlines.
  • Validate migration completion: Review migration status and confirm that important Whiteboards, permissions, and user access have been successfully migrated and remain accessible in OneDrive-backed storage.
  • Plan for large-scale migrations: For inactive users, orphaned Whiteboards, or large migration volumes, consider using the administrator-driven migration approach documented by Microsoft Whiteboard engineering.
  • Update internal guidance: Update user training materials, help documentation, and support procedures to direct users to Microsoft Whiteboard in Teams and supported web experiences rather than standalone applications.
  • Act before migration tooling is retired: After September 25, 2026, migration tooling will no longer be available, and no further migration path will exist for remaining legacy Whiteboards.

This feature helps organizations that work with external event producers, agencies, and third-party event management partners by allowing authorized external presenters to perform production tasks without requiring internal staff to manage the event.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 567298.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in early August 2026 and expected to complete by early October 2026 (previously early September) (previously mid-August)
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning early August 2026 and expected to complete by early October 2026 (previously early September)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that use Microsoft Teams events
  • Event organizers who work with external presenters, production vendors, agencies, or trusted partners
  • Federated (B2B) users and guest users who are invited to participate in Teams events

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams events

What will happen

  • Event organizers can grant production control permissions to federated (B2B) users and guest users.
  • Authorized external presenters can manage production controls and determine what attendees see during an event.
  • The feature is available only when an organizer explicitly assigns production control access.
  • Existing events and configurations will not be modified automatically.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required before rollout.

We recommend that you:

  • Review internal guidance and governance policies for Teams events that include external participants.
  • Inform event organizers about this new capability.
  • Determine which external presenters, vendors, or partners should be authorized to receive production control permissions.
  • Update any training or documentation used by event organizers, if applicable.

Organizers can use the Who has control of production tools setting when configuring a Teams event to grant production access to trusted external users.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change provide a new way for users, tenants, or subscriptions to communicate?Yes. This feature enables organizations to include federated (B2B) and guest users in Teams event production workflows, expanding collaboration and communication capabilities with trusted external participants.
Does this change include an admin or organizer control?Yes. Event organizers can use the Who has control of production tools setting to grant or restrict production control access for trusted external users when configuring a Teams event.
Can users enable or disable this capability themselves?Yes. Event organizers can choose whether to grant production control permissions to federated (B2B) and guest users when setting up an event.

item.title: [planForChange] Support for Office LTSC 2021, and additional apps will end on October 13, 2026
item.description:
[What and why:]

As previously communicated, support for Office LTSC 2021 will end on October 13, 2026. After that date, no further updates, security fixes, or technical support will be available for this version of Office. While the applications may continue to function, using unsupported software could lead to potential security risks, compliance risks, system incompatibilities, and other issues.

Support for Visio LTSC 2021, Microsoft Project LTSC 2021 and several other products will also end on October 13, 2026. Organizations using these products should upgrade as soon as possible to maintain security, compliance, and performance.

[Rollout schedule:]

We will begin rolling out mid-October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

After end of support, Office LTSC 2021 suites and standalones will no longer receive security updates or other fixes, and no technical assistance will be available for devices still running them. Continuing to use unsupported software can expose your organization to security and compliance risks and may impact service reliability and performance.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

To mitigate these risks while maintaining access to desktop Office apps, we recommend upgrading devices to a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 suite that includes Microsoft 365 Apps (for enterprise or for business). Microsoft 365 Apps provides always-up-to-date versions of familiar apps like Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for desktop, mobile, and web with continuous support under the Modern Lifecycle Policy, and is eligible for use with the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on.

  • Enterprises should look to Microsoft 365 E3, Office 365 E3, or Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.
  • Organizations with fewer than 300 users should look to Microsoft 365 Business Premium, Microsoft 365 Business Standard, or Microsoft 365 Apps for business.

For scenarios that require a fully disconnected solution, we recommend upgrading to Office LTSC 2024. Office LTSC 2024 is Microsoft’s current supported on-premises version of Office for commercial customers and will be supported until October 2029 under the Fixed Lifecycle Policy.

Take steps to prepare for this transition with the following resources:

  1. Read the upgrade guidance for an overview of how to move from Office LTSC 2021 to Microsoft 365 Apps. 
  2. Consider engaging Microsoft FastTrack, a Microsoft support service, for moving to Microsoft 365. 

Take action before October 13, 2026, to help maintain security, compliance, and access to supported Office apps.
